title: Threading bug - race condition in uv_async_send
body:
* **Version**: 1.27
* **Platform**: linux / maybe macos

I've spent the last few days tracking down [a race condition in the foundationdb node bindings](https://github.com/josephg/node-foundationdb/issues/28). Foundationdb owns a networking thread. Behaviour is like this:

1. Nodejs calls an async database function (fetch data / whatever)
2. We create a `uv_async`, associated with a foundationdb future object
3. Foundationdb signals that the work is completed by calling a method on its networking thread
4. We call `uv_async_send` on the associated async object
5. In the main thread, data is returned to nodejs and the async object is deallocated

[relevant code in node-foundationdb is here](https://github.com/josephg/node-foundationdb/blob/d24483918a45e56572c88e804444c158d354b734/src/future.cpp#L16-L47).

(I know this is an inefficient use of `uv_async` - I'll rewrite all this code when we move to napi).

This code is crashing sometimes, and I can't figure out exactly why. The call to `uv_async_send` has a use-after-free bug - sometimes the `uv_async` has been deleted before `uv_async_send` returns, and the call to `uv_async_send` crashes. (But reading the code, I don't understand how this is possible). The original bug (in the linked issue) only seems to trigger on linux after running for about 20 minutes.

I made a [pure C / libuv repro](https://gist.github.com/josephg/d646cc4fdbb89ff0a19ec6c5c5550969) of this issue which crashes reliably in less than a minute on macos and linux. I'm not 100% sure this repro code is correct, but it crashes in the same way so I think so.

Am I using libuv correctly? It seems weird that I'm the first person to run into this bug.
